name: Starter: Russian
about: Russian word order and cases in real, everyday sentences.

words.идти: to go or come on foot; to leave
words.дело: matter, thing (как дела: how are things)
words.звать: to call (меня зовут: my name is)
words.нравиться: to appeal to, to please (мне нравится: I like it)
words.можно: it's possible, it's allowed; may, can
words.ехать: to go (by car, bus or train)
words.пойти: to set off; to go (one trip)

как-дела.about: A friendly greeting: literally, how things? Answer with Хорошо, спасибо (fine, thanks).

как-тебя-зовут.about: Literally, how do they call you? Answer with Меня зовут and your name.

извините.about: To get someone's attention, or to say sorry.

дай-мне-знать.about: A fixed request: tell me, keep me posted.

у-меня-есть.about: Literally, at me there is. Есть is often left out when what matters is what something is like, not whether it's there: У меня большая комната.

concept.line: The verb changes for each person: я живу, ты живёшь, он живёт, мы живём, они живут.
Russian leaves out am, is and are in the present: Я студент (I'm a student); Где мои ключи?

Most nouns ending in a consonant are masculine, most in -а or -я feminine and most in -о or -е neuter (though words for men stay masculine: папа), and adjectives, possessives such as мой and a singular past-tense verb agree with them.

A yes/no question keeps the order of a statement, with the voice rising on the word asked about (Ты говоришь по-английски?), a question word like как, где or что often comes first, and Russian adds no do.
A direct object often takes the accusative (Мы ели пиццу); so does where you're going after в or на (в магазин, на работу), and many expressions of time (в субботу).

words.means: живу = live; живёшь = live; живёт = lives
иду = am going; идёшь = are going; идёт = is going

concept.line: To say you have something, Russian says it is at you: У меня есть брат (I have a brother); when what matters is what it's like, not whether it's there, есть is often left out: У меня большая комната.

words.means: to go or come on foot; to leave
